notes:
Background: SignalHarbor runs a multi-tenant support platform for mid-to-enterprise SaaS vendors. Goal is to reduce live-agent volume via RAG ticket deflection + a fast support assistant embedded in their web console.

Key quotes: 'Top-5 must be relevant — if the first 5 results don't help, we escalate' — Head of Support. 'Need sub-200ms median for search flow, 95th < 350ms for production' — Platform lead.

What they're measuring: query latency (median + 95th), cost per query (tokens + embedding lookup + rerank costs), top-5 relevance (NDCG@5 / manual eval), index freshness (near-realtime for new KB articles).

Technical constraints: mixed content types (markdown KB, attachments PDF/OCR, ticket transcripts). ~20M indexed docs expected at scale. They want prefix caching for conversational contexts, vector index + ANN for candidate retrieval, then a lightweight cross-encoder or learned reranker for top-5 quality. Prefer model variants that can run on dedicated GPUs with quantization.

Security/compliance: must support corporate SSO (SAML/SCIM), audit logs for query content, allow customer-managed KMS, and EU data residency for some customers.

Engagement to date: discovery -> architecture review -> POC planning. They requested specific perf targets and a TCO analysis comparing Redwood Dedicated vs self-hosted + Pinecone.

Open items: final legal wording for data residency, acceptance criteria for POC (latency + quality thresholds), and cost model for burst vs sustained traffic.

Emphasis on cost per query optimization via batching, caching, and quantized models.

Cost target: <$0.015 per query (at scale) including embedding & rerank
Model preferences: open LLMs quantized, ability to pin a model, fallback routing
